evidence: The original win32 entry was `{ command: "cmd", args: ["/c", "start", ""] }`, so cmd.exe re-parses the URL and `&` in a query string becomes a command separator. The agent took the reviewer's explorer.exe option and declined escaping; cff610a shows that change plus a hostile-URL test.
guidance_note: Before handing an externally sourced string to a child process, check whether the destination binary is an interpreter (cmd, sh), and pick a launcher that takes the value as a plain argument.

evidence: The original code spawned with no `error` listener, and Node throws an unlistened ChildProcess error as an uncaught exception. Rather than calling app.notify from the service, the agent made spawnUrlOpener return a rejecting promise that App.openUrl reports, which keeps the leaf service from depending on App.
guidance_note: An unlistened `error` event crashes the process; it is not a loud failure. Before citing no-silent-failure for a missing handler, trace where the error actually goes.

evidence: The diagnosis was right: the mount effect called `setUrlOpener(undefined)` and reset a host's opener. The reviewer's cure, forwarding `appOptions.openUrl` through render() into TextualApp, built the App→React→App round trip that produced F18 and F20. The agent deleted that forwarding in 8b1c0b9 and wrote that `App.urlOpener` should be the authority, with `AppOptions.openUrl` only its initial value.
guidance_note: When two writers race over one field, find the single authority before you thread a value through another layer. A value that leaves an object and comes back to it through a prop is a second writer.

evidence: This duplicates F2. The reviewer asked for an error listener that surfaces through the app's notification path, and cff610a does that: the promise rejects and App.openUrl calls notify.
guidance_note: An unlistened `error` event crashes the process; it is not a loud failure. Before citing no-silent-failure for a missing handler, trace where the error actually goes.

evidence: cff610a wrote `void Promise.resolve(this.urlOpener(url)).catch(...)` and widened UrlOpener to `void | Promise<void>`. A synchronous throw unwinds while the argument is evaluated, before the catch is attached. 21cd164 moved the call into `.then()` and added a test with a throwing opener.
guidance_note: When wrapping a call to catch its failures, put the invocation inside the promise chain or try block, and test the fix with a double that throws synchronously as well as one that rejects.

evidence: This duplicates F5: the same synchronous-throw hole in the cff610a `Promise.resolve(this.urlOpener(url))` wrapper, and the same 21cd164 fix.
guidance_note: When wrapping a call to catch its failures, put the invocation inside the promise chain or try block, and test the fix with a double that throws synchronously as well as one that rejects.

evidence: This duplicates F5. It adds that the throw propagates through BindingDispatcher.runAction, which re-throws anything that is not SkipAction, so the comment's claim that a failed open won't tear down the TUI was false for sync openers. Fixed in 21cd164.
guidance_note: When wrapping a call to catch its failures, put the invocation inside the promise chain or try block, and test the fix with a double that throws synchronously as well as one that rejects.

evidence: The fourth copy of the synchronous-throw finding on the cff610a wrapper. 21cd164's `Promise.resolve().then(() => this.urlOpener(url))` closes it.
guidance_note: When wrapping a call to catch its failures, put the invocation inside the promise chain or try block, and test the fix with a double that throws synchronously as well as one that rejects.

evidence: The F1 fix removed shell reinterpretation but still passed any string, including UNC paths and file: URLs, to open/explorer.exe/xdg-open. The agent's own F1 reply had called the url externally sourced. 21cd164 added parseOpenableUrl with an http/https/mailto allowlist and made urlOpenCommand take a URL, which matches the reviewer's suggestion.
guidance_note: Once you call an input untrusted to justify one fix, list every way that input can hurt at that sink (interpretation, target, scheme) and close them in the same commit.

evidence: cff610a resolved on the `spawn` event, so xdg-open exiting non-zero with no $DISPLAY reported success, which contradicts the comment that failures reject. 21cd164 settles on `exit` and carries per-platform `exitCodeReportsFailure` as data, with explorer.exe false. The agent declined stderr capture, which the reviewer had offered only as a nice-to-have.
guidance_note: When a fix claims every failure is reported, enumerate the launcher's failure modes (never spawns, spawns then exits non-zero, never exits) and pick the settle event that covers them all.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: `target = url ?? content.plain` and the optional `text` prop are original Link code, and cff610a did not touch link-component.tsx. The agent took the reviewer's first option (`text` required, matching Textual's mandatory positional) and relied on parseOpenableUrl rejecting "" rather than adding a skip guard, which the 21cd164 test shows.
guidance_note: When porting a widget, carry over which constructor arguments the reference makes required instead of making every prop optional.

evidence: This duplicates F11, and the flag is a false positive for the same reason: Link's target computation is pre-review code. Required `text` plus the scheme checkpoint resolved it, and the agent declined a silent `if (target)` skip.
guidance_note: When porting a widget, carry over which constructor arguments the reference makes required instead of making every prop optional.

evidence: 21cd164 added the exit-code settle logic and tested only the pure halves, saying 'The spawn itself is the untestable half'. The agent extracted runUrlOpenCommand, tested it against real child processes, and found that the extraction had made spawnUrlOpener throw synchronously; marking it async fixed that.
guidance_note: When a fix adds effectful branching, extract a seam that takes the command as input and test each outcome against a real child process in the same commit.

evidence: cff610a introduced `this.notify(`Could not open ${url}: ...`, "error")`, and markup defaults to true there, so brackets in a URL such as `https://[::1]:8080/` are parsed as markup. The agent switched to `{ severity: "error", markup: false }`, the same choice the PR already made for Link text.
guidance_note: When interpolating external data into any markup-rendering API, pass the no-markup option at the call site, as already done for Link text in the same PR.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. The openUrl useLayoutEffect in textual-app.tsx was in the original PR (its hunk is against the base), and 21cd164 did not touch that file, so the stale header enumeration dates from round 0. The agent appended 'url opener' to the list.
guidance_note: When adding a member to a set that a header comment enumerates, update the enumeration in the same edit.

evidence: The test 21cd164 added for F11 declares `opened` but never wires it to an opener, so `expect(opened).toEqual([])` cannot fail. The agent deleted it, pinned the 'Not a URL' message, and explained why wiring a spy would invert the test: the scheme check lives only in the default opener.
guidance_note: Before claiming a test covers a fix, break the code under test and confirm the test fails; check that every collector the test asserts on is actually wired.

evidence: The 21cd164 diff of tests/url-opener.test.ts shows the new scheme-checkpoint comment added under the old 'platform decision is split out' comment, which was left in place. The agent deleted the stale pair.
guidance_note: When rewriting a comment, replace the old one rather than adding the new version beside it; reread the diff hunk for duplicated prose before committing.

evidence: After cff610a, `new App(); app.setUrlOpener(custom); app.render()` still lost the custom opener: the mount passed `appOptions.openUrl`, which was undefined, and `opener ?? spawnUrlOpener` reset it. The agent changed absence to mean keep. That fixed this sequence but left the round trip, which F20 then found. The agent later wrote 'I fixed the instance rather than the cause last round.'
guidance_note: When a fix leaves two writers to one field, enumerate every ordering of writes (options, setter, mount) and test each one before pushing.

evidence: The runUrlOpenCommand tests added for F13 spawned `true`/`false`, which native Windows lacks. That platform is the one whose `exitCodeReportsFailure: false` rule the tests exist to pin. 8b1c0b9 switched to `process.execPath -e process.exit(n)`.
guidance_note: When a test pins platform-specific behaviour, use fixtures that exist on that platform (node itself, not coreutils).

evidence: `opener ?? this.urlOpener` still let a defined `AppOptions.openUrl`, sent back through render() and the mount, overwrite a later pre-render setUrlOpener(B). The reviewer offered a comment note or a reconciling mount effect. The agent instead deleted the render() forwarding (8b1c0b9) and added the A-then-B test.
guidance_note: When a fix leaves two writers to one field, enumerate every ordering of writes (options, setter, mount) and test each one before pushing.

evidence: cff610a appended `openUrl?: UrlOpener` directly under the comment saying env and driver are 'not separately stored on App', which is false for openUrl. 8b1c0b9 moved it above that block and gave it its own note.
guidance_note: When inserting a field into a commented group, check that the group comment's claims hold for the new member, or place the field outside the group.

evidence: Moving the settle from `spawn` to `exit` in 21cd164 means a handler that runs in the foreground (xdg-open into w3m or mutt) never settles; before that change it resolved on spawn. The agent bounded the wait but resolves rather than rejects at the window, arguing that rejecting would raise a false error on a cold-starting browser. The reasoning holds, and the fix shipped in 63d12ab.
guidance_note: When switching a promise to settle on process exit, ask what happens if the process never exits, and bound the wait in the same change.

narrative: The PR adds a Link widget and an App-owned URL opener. The reviewer's round-0 findings were all real: Windows shell injection, the missing error listener crashing the app, and the opener being clobbered on mount. But each fix shipped its own next finding. The promise wrapper missed synchronous throws (four duplicate findings). Resolving on spawn missed launchers that start and then fail, and switching to exit later caused an unbounded wait. The new spawn logic was untested, and when tests came their fixtures did not run on Windows. Forwarding openUrl through render() created an App→React→App round trip that took two more rounds to remove, ending in deletion of the forwarding the agent had accepted from the reviewer in round 0. Rounds 3 and 4 contained only fix-caused findings, and round 5 was cut off by the review cap.
guidance_observations: Taking the reviewer's local cure for the clobber (forward through render) cost two rounds; the agent's eventual root-cause fix (App is the sole authority) was available at round 0.
Twice the agent found a test it wrote for a fix was vacuous or caught a new bug on first run (F13, and F22's sleep fixture), which is evidence for mutation-checking every fix test before pushing.

Each fix to the opener's settle semantics introduced the next failure mode (sync throw, spawn-vs-exit, never-exits); listing the failure modes once up front would have collapsed three rounds into one.

evidence: The getters read `this.screen?.title`, but `activeScreen` is a computed that returns the same Screen object after an in-place retitle, so MobX suppresses the notification. The PR's own activeTitleOverride comment says so. 6c5f477 routed both getters through activeTitleOverride, and the agent reported an observer test that fails on revert.
guidance_note: When you have written a workaround for a reactivity trap, grep the same PR for every other read of the trapped value and route those reads through the workaround too.

evidence: The ScreenOptions comment claimed Textual's Screen.TITLE class attribute, but createScreen read only `options.title`. The agent cited the spec line 'If the screen defines a TITLE, it overrides App.TITLE' and implemented `options.title ?? screenType.TITLE ?? null` in 6c5f477.
guidance_note: When a comment claims parity with a reference attribute, implement the read the same way neighbouring statics such as AUTO_FOCUS are read, or don't make the claim.

evidence: `options.title ?? this.constructor.name` keeps "", but Python's `TITLE or __class__.__name__` falls back on it. 6c5f477 switched to `||`, narrowed the comment to construction time, and added a test.
guidance_note: When porting Python `x or y`, translate it as `||`, not `??`, unless you deliberately want empty values to survive, and say so.

evidence: The comment said the Screen 'can be handed straight to resolveTitle'. That type-checks and would reintroduce the stale-reference bug that activeTitleOverride avoids by building a fresh object. 6c5f477 deleted the claim and pointed readers to activeTitleOverride.
guidance_note: Don't document a structural-typing convenience that your own workaround elsewhere exists to avoid; check each comment against the reasoning in neighbouring comments.

evidence: This is the same defect as F1 (stale reads through `this.screen?.title`). One 6c5f477 change fixed both, and the agent reported an observer-based test that bites on revert.
guidance_note: When you have written a workaround for a reactivity trap, grep the same PR for every other read of the trapped value and route those reads through the workaround too.

evidence: `leading = Math.floor(slack/2)` puts the odd cell on the trailing side, the opposite of what the comment said. The 6c5f477 diff rewrites the comment to 'An odd remainder goes to the trailing side'.
guidance_note: Check a directional claim in a comment against one odd-valued example of the arithmetic before committing it.

evidence: The F5 fix closed the stale read in App's getters, but the public `App.screen` still exposed mutable `title`/`subTitle`, so `app.screen.title = "X"` bypassed the version bump. 6c5f477 had only added a comment saying 'never off the Screen'. e6f6634 made the fields readonly with a private mutable alias.
guidance_note: When closing one bypass of an owner's write path, list every public handle to the same object (getters such as App.screen) and close the bypass at the type.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. The `resolvedTitle` getter and its ResolvedTitle return type predate review (round 0 describes them), so the missing export was an original gap, not something 6c5f477 caused. e6f6634 exported the type through both barrels.
guidance_note: When adding a public getter or hook, export its parameter and return types through the same barrels as the sibling API it claims parity with.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the gap was in the original test file. Only the pure resolveTitle test defended the empty-subtitle override. e6f6634 added a rendered case, and the agent reported it fails under the `||` regression.
guidance_note: For each distinction a type exists to preserve, write a rendered end-to-end test alongside the pure-function test.

evidence: 6c5f477 narrowed the app.tsx comment to 'the guarantee is about construction' but left the divergences doc saying 'a Header always has a title to paint'. e6f6634 added the matching qualifier to the doc.
guidance_note: When narrowing a claim in source, grep the docs for the same claim and narrow it in the same commit.

evidence: 6c5f477 implemented the static TITLE read for Screen but not for App, though the App comment claims `App.TITLE or __class__.__name__` parity. The agent agreed it was 'the same gap I just closed one layer down', and e6f6634 added resolveStaticTitle and resolveStaticSubTitle.
guidance_note: When implementing a static-attribute read for one class in response to a finding, apply it to every class that declares the same attribute name before pushing.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the `constructor.name` fallback was in the round-0 code, and 6c5f477 only changed `??` to `||`. The minification risk is real but narrow, and the reviewer asked only for a note. e6f6634 added one to the divergences doc.

The flag is a false positive. useResolvedTitle, and its comment claiming parity with useBindings, were original code, so the missing export predates 6c5f477. e6f6634 exported the hook through both barrels.

evidence: e6f6634 made the Screen title fields readonly, which blocked writes, but `app.screen?.title` reads inside an observer were still stale for the same reference-comparer reason. 600e40d removed the fields from Screen and added an internal TitledScreen. The agent conceded: 'I closed the write and left the read'.
guidance_note: When a field on a public shape is unsafe to use, take it off the public type rather than making it readonly; check that reads are safe as well as writes.

evidence: e6f6634 extended the constructor comment with a blanket '`||`, not `??`' rule, directly above a new subTitle line that uses `??`. 600e40d scoped the rule to title and stated why subTitle uses `??`.
guidance_note: When a comment states a rule above two lines, check that both lines follow it, or explain the exception in place.

evidence: The F9 fix added an empty-override test for subTitle only. title goes through the same `??` in resolveTitle, and a title-only `||` regression passed every test. 600e40d added the pure and rendered title cases.

evidence: e6f6634 exported resolveTitle and NO_TITLE_OVERRIDE as values from framework/index.ts, but src/index.ts forwarded only the types. 600e40d forwarded the values.

evidence: e6f6634 added `options.subTitle ?? resolveStaticSubTitle() ?? ""` but tested only the title precedence. 600e40d added constructor-beats-static and explicit-empty-survives tests for subTitle, and the agent reported the second fails under `||`.

evidence: The screenTitle JSDoc from 6c5f477 says reading `this.screen.title` 'would type-check'. After 600e40d removed title from Screen, that read is a compile error. 1848c3d trimmed the paragraph.

evidence: This duplicates F19: the same stale 'would type-check' JSDoc after the 600e40d TitledScreen change, fixed by the same 1848c3d rewrite.
guidance_note: After hardening a type, grep for comments that argue about the old weakness and update them in the same commit.

evidence: 600e40d added resolveTitle and NO_TITLE_OVERRIDE to src/index.ts, but the tests still imported them from framework/title-resolution.js, so no test exercised the new export. The agent switched the imports and reported that removing the exports now fails three tests.
guidance_note: When adding an export to fix an API gap, import it from the public entry point in the tests so the export is exercised.

narrative: The PR adds screen-over-app title resolution and a Header. Round 0's six findings were all real and pre-existing. Every round-2 and round-3 finding came from an incomplete round-0 or round-1 fix. The stale-title bug was closed for App's getters, then for writes through `app.screen`, then for reads through it, and finally left a stale JSDoc. Fixes were applied to one of two symmetric items and the other was found next round: Screen TITLE but not App TITLE, the subTitle test but not title, type exports but not values. The agent's responses were consistently correct and well verified; the cost was entirely in fixes that did not sweep their own class.
guidance_observations: Three chains here are 'fixed one of a symmetric pair' (Screen vs App TITLE, subTitle vs title test, types vs values export); a pre-push sweep for the twin of each change would have removed round 2.

The agent repeatedly said a comment was doing a type's job, yet still shipped readonly first and type removal a round later; closing both read and write at the type on the first pass would have saved a round.
Three comments outlived the code they described (F10, F15, F19/20); after each fix, grep for prose that argues about the old behaviour.
